summary: Peter James Gilks specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under several traditional teachers, and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (attested 2010).

Peter K. Austin is a linguist who earned his PhD from the Australian National University (1975–1978). He served as Foundation Professor in Linguistics at the University of Melbourne (1996–2002) and Emeritus Professor in Field Linguistics at SOAS University of London (2002–2018).

Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter Kuhlmann is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rosemarie Lühr (~1990–1993) and held posts at the University of Giessen (~2001–2002), University of Düsseldorf (~2002–2004), and University of Göttingen (~2004).

Peter Lindegger-Stauffer (1933–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was Curator at the Tibet Institute Rikon from 1967 to 1974 and received an honorary Ph.D. from the University of Fribourg in ~1998.

Peter M. Scharf works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania (1983–1990) under George Cardona. He founded the Sanskrit Library (2002) and held posts at Penn, Brown, IIIT Hyderabad, and IIAS.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and doctoral supervisor Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and the University of Washington (PhD), working under doctoral supervisor Charles Keyes alongside several other academic and traditional teachers.

Peter N. Gregory is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at UIUC, Komazawa University, the Kuroda Institute, and Smith College.

Peter Nicolas Harting (1892–1970) worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his M.A. and Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Willem Caland. He held posts at the University of London, Bedford College, Oxford, and was Professor of English at Groningen and Amsterdam.
Peter Pasedach is an Indologist. He has held posts at Utkal University (attested 2022) and the University of Hamburg as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).

Peter Percival (1803–1882) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Principal of Jaffna Central College (1832–1851), taught at St Augustine's College (~1854–1856), and became Registrar at the University of Madras and Professor at Presidency University in 1856.

Peter Peterson (1847–1899) was an Indologist who studied at Edinburgh and Oxford under Theodor Aufrecht, Monier Monier-Williams, and Friedrich Max Müller. He served at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and was President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. After studying at Temple, Münster (Promotion under Paul Hacker), and Tübingen (Habilitation), he held posts at Tübingen, SOAS, and the University of Zurich, becoming Professor in 1990 and later Professor Emeritus.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his M.A. in 1994 at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, studying under Dieter Schuh. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Bonn, where he held the Lehrstuhl für Tibetologie.

Peter Scott Noble (1899–1987) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Aberdeen and St John's College, Cambridge, and held academic appointments at Liverpool, Leeds, Aberdeen, King's College London, and the University of London.

Peter Skilling specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the EPHE and founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation. He has held positions at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and visiting roles at Harvard, Oxford, UC Berkeley, and Sydney.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Clare College, Cambridge. He held positions at Cambridge, Reading, Ure Museum, Courtauld Institute, and the University of Oxford, where he became Associate Professor in 2011.

Peter Stumpf (1940–1977) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Goethe University Frankfurt (1959–1968) under Werner Thomas and served as an Assistant there from ~1968 to 1977.
